title: Tanzanian Coconut Cake
community: Urban Tanzania and Zanzibar — the celebration cake
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Keki ya Nazi — a moist, tender coconut milk cake with a fragrant cardamom crumb, topped with a coconut cream frosting and toasted desiccated coconut. The Tanzanian celebration cake — all the flavours of the coast in a single slice.
longDesc: Coconut cake is Tanzania's modern celebration dessert — the Western cake format completely transformed by the island's coconut and cardamom. Made for birthdays, wedding receptions, and graduation parties across urban Tanzania and Zanzibar, it is the cake that most represents the country's contemporary food identity.
ingredients: // Topping: ½ cup desiccated coconut — toasted golden
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and line cake tin.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, cardamom, and salt.
In a separate bowl, beat eggs and sugar until pale — 3 minutes.
Add coconut milk, oil, vanilla, and lime zest. Mix.
Fold wet into dry until just combined — do not over-mix.
Pour into tin. Bake 35—40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Frosting: whip chilled coconut cream with icing sugar and vanilla until fluffy.
Frost the cooled cake. Press toasted coconut all over.
chefTips: Do not over-mix the batter — creates a tough crumb.
The coconut cream must be refrigerated overnight for the frosting to whip properly.
Lime zest in the batter is the brightness that lifts the whole cake.
commonMistakes: Frosting a warm cake — frosting melts.
Coconut cream not chilled — will not whip.
cookingScience: The high fat content of coconut milk tenderises the cake crumb by coating the gluten strands — inhibiting their development and producing a more tender, moist crumb than a plain milk cake. Chilled coconut cream whips because the coconut fat crystallises when cold, creating a stable foam similar to whipped cream.
sustainabilityTips: Zanzibar coconut milk and cream — locally produced.
reheating: Room temperature — serve at room temp.
culturalNote: Coconut cake is Tanzania's modern celebration — the traditional coastal flavours (coconut, cardamom, lime) expressed in the universal language of birthday cake. At every Tanzanian birthday table, the coconut cake is the most requested.
